Germany’s rearmament is not designed to make the country more militarily sovereign — for better or worse. It is designed to elevate Germany’s role as the “vassal-in-chief” within the US-controlled NATO command structure. In this sense, the Trump-Merz spat should be seen as little more than political theatre. The US is not “disengaging from Europe”; it is simply demanding that Europe contribute more to NATO, while remaining firmly embedded within the alliance’s command structure — in short, that it pays more for its own subordination. In this light, the ostensible US “threats” to leave NATO — and the European establishment’s rearmament programme, Germany’s above all — are revealed as components of the same strategy: keeping Europe subordinated to American geopolitical priorities. The new German military strategy is nothing more than Berlin fulfilling the role Washington has assigned it: holding the line against Russia while the US turns towards the Indo-Pacific and the Western Hemisphere. This is not nationalism, military or otherwise, but its opposite: the undermining of German and European core interests at the hands of a transnationalised globalist elite — Merz is, after all, a former BlackRock executive — that views permanent war and militarisation as a way to entrench its wealth and power at the expense of European prosperity and security. German and European rearmament, in the context of a supposedly more “European” NATO, is not strengthening European autonomy, but further eroding it. Not only does it make Europe complicit in Washington’s increasingly reckless military adventures, as the Iran war demonstrates, but more gravely still, it is pushing the continent towards a potentially catastrophic confrontation with Russia. Hukuk devletinin, hukukun üstünlüğünün, iyi yönetim ilkelerinin temel dayanağı anayasal metinlerdir. Kanun-i Esasi’yi takip eden dört anayasaya rağmen Türk milletinin iyi bir anayasa özlemi hâlen dinmemiştir. Kurucu anayasalarımız dışında son iki anayasanın maalesef darbelerin, hukuk dışı müdahalelerin ürünü olmasının bunda payı büyüktür. Bu demokratik ayıbı gidermek, Türk siyasetinin boynunun borcudur. Yeni, kuşatıcı, özgürlükçü ve sivil bir anayasa, demokrasimizi aşağıdan yukarıya doğru inşa etmenin imkânıyla önümüzde duruyor. Anayasayı, darbecilerin veya seçkinlerin belirleyip topluma dayattıkları bir çerçeve olmaktan çıkarıp toplumun kendisinin belirleyip devlete deklare ettiği bir metne dönüştürmek zorundayız. İnanıyorum ki böyle bir anayasa ile hem hukuku hem demokrasiyi hem devleti hem de milleti aynı anda koruyacak bir üstün hukuk mantığına kavuşmamız mümkün olacaktır. Biz bu konuyu her türlü siyasi matematik hesabının üstünde, zihnimizde ve reform gündemimizin üst sıralarında tutmaya devam edeceğiz.

At the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi, Kenya, co-hosted by President @WilliamsRuto and President @EmmanuelMacron, I shared my thoughts and Ethiopia’s experience during the session on Green Industrialization and Energy Transition. Ethiopia continues to play a key role in these two areas.

Met with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva @KGeorgieva this morning and exchanged views on economic progress, partnership, and shared priorities. Grateful for the insightful conversation and continued engagement.

During the opening of the Africa Forward Summit at KICC, Nairobi, co-chaired with President Emmanuel Macron of France. Present were Presidents @PaulKagame (Rwanda), @AOuattara_PRCI (Côte d’Ivoire), @AlsisiOfficial (Egypt), @FA_Touadera (Central African Republic), @PR_AZALI (Comoros), Mohamed Ould Ghazouani (Mauritania), Mohamed al-Menfi (Libya), and King Letsie III (Lesotho). Also present are Hakainde Hichilema (Zambia), Mamady Doumbouya (Guinea), Bola Ahmed Tinubu (Nigeria), Joseph Boakai (Liberia), Bassirou Diomaye Faye (Senegal), Mahamat Idriss Déby (Chad), Duma Boko (Botswana), Dharambeer Gokhool (Mauritius), @JDMahama (Ghana), Daniel Chapo (Mozambique), and Michael Randrianirina (Madagascar), Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (Ethiopia), and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres. Others are Prime Ministers Aziz Akhannouch (Morocco), Russell Dlamini (Eswatini), Américo Ramos (São Tomé and Príncipe) Sara Zaafarani Zenzri (Tunisia), Mwigulu Nchemba (Tanzania), and African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf. Vice-Presidents, ambassadors, heads of delegations, country representatives and development partners, among others, also attended the summit.

The times before us demand strong cooperation, renewed multilateralism and partnerships grounded not in hierarchy, but mutual respect and shared responsibility. It is in this spirit that we convened this summit in our shared conviction that enduring partnerships must not be built on dependence but on sovereign equity, not on aid or charity but mutually beneficial investments, and not on extraction or exploitation but on win-win engagements.

We are clear on what we must achieve to unlock Africa’s vast potential and drive transformation. This includes domestic mobilisation of resources for Africa’s development at scale, reform of the international financial architecture, development of transport, and logistics and connectivity infrastructure. Others are energy transition and green industrialisation, and youth skills development to foster creativity, innovation, entrepreneurship and AI-driven transformation.

Using a mix of propaganda, disinformation, physical and cyber threats, cognitive warfare seeks to alter perceptions, emotions and behaviour, and ultimately, sow chaos. Under a barrage of cognitive warfare, European governments need institutions designed to interpret threats, coordinate responses and act fast. Yet Europe’s defence architecture is built for a different era—one of clear enemies, distinct timelines and identifiable campaigns. On the sidelines of the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi, Minister @onduhungirehe attended a Ministerial-Level Strategic Dialogue on UN Security Council Reform and the Use of Veto. In his remarks, he said that, for a long time, the use of veto rights or the threat of its use has repeatedly been employed to pressure member states or block serious consideration of humanitarian interventions, thereby paralyzing the Council’s primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. He, therefore, reiterated Rwanda’s alignment with the Common African Position, which advocates for equitable representation of Africa on the UN Security Council. The Minister also emphasized that structural reform must go hand in hand with reforms to the Council’s working methods, including improvements in transparency and accountability.

At the CII Annual Business Summit 2026, Shri Rajiv Gauba delivered a Special Address during the session on “Institutionalising Reform – Building the Structural Foundation for India’s Future Economy”, organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry. “Every nation has its moments of opportunity, and India stands at one today,” said Shri Rajiv Gauba. Highlighting India as the world’s fastest growing major economy, he noted that the country has the demographics, digital infrastructure, market scale, and political commitment needed to attract global investment. Shri Rajiv Gauba stressed the need to reduce “regulatory cholesterol” and remove excessive clearances, renewals, and permissions that act as licensing by another name. He noted that the next generation of reforms must move governance from suspicion to trust, and from “prohibited unless permitted” to “permitted unless prohibited”, the essence of Jan Vishwas. Shri Rajiv Gauba noted that early reform outcomes are already visible, with 1.2 lakh hectares of industrial land unlocked, thousands of small businesses freed from unnecessary licensing, and compliance burdens reduced across sectors. He emphasised that industry must also strengthen investment in innovation and skilling, with India’s R&D spending at 0.7% of GDP and private sector contribution at around 36%. Highlighting the needs of Industry 4.0, he called for accelerated industry-led skilling initiatives, noting that only 20% of construction workers and 1% of hospitality workers are formally skilled. He stated that “a rising GDP is the best foreign policy” and stressed the need for urgency and shared purpose to realise India’s growth potential. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #CIIAnnualBusinessSummit2026 #JanVishwas #EaseOfDoingBusiness #EconomicReforms

Nestled in the hills of Northeast India, Nagaland is a land defined by its vibrant tribal heritage and deeply rooted traditions. Home to diverse indigenous communities, each with its own customs, language, and attire, the state reflects a rich cultural identity that continues to thrive in everyday life. From the dynamic celebrations of the Hornbill Festival to the unique village experiences of Khonoma and Longwa, Nagaland offers a glimpse into traditions that are preserved through generations. Its cultural expressions are visible in its music, dance, crafts, and community-driven lifestyle. The cuisine, featuring smoked meats, bamboo shoot dishes, and fermented flavours like axone, represents a bold and authentic culinary identity. Handcrafted textiles, beadwork, and woodcraft further showcase the artistic traditions that are closely tied to tribal identity. Surrounded by rolling hills, valleys, and forests, Nagaland also offers scenic landscapes that complement its cultural richness. Whether it is engaging with local communities or experiencing its festivals, the state offers a journey that is immersive and culturally enriching. An initiative of NITI Aayog, Divya Bharat – A Window to the Soul of India is a curated national effort to showcase the country’s diverse cultural, spiritual, and natural heritage. Through a state-wise journey, it brings together India’s rich traditions, iconic landscapes, vibrant festivals, and living heritage, offering a holistic narrative of the nation’s unity in diversity. Building India’s AI Infrastructure Sovereignty for the Frontier AI Era The article by Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, highlights the need for India to build digital infrastructure sovereignty as frontier AI systems become central to cybersecurity, benchmarking, risk assessment, and crisis-response capacity. Using Anthropic’s Claude Mythos Preview as a case study, the piece underscores that access to frontier technologies is shaped by jurisdiction, institutional relationships, infrastructure depth, national-security alignment, and established trust. It further emphasizes the importance of strengthening capabilities across compute, chips, cloud, data, standards, evaluation capacity, and AI safety institutions. The article calls for a long-term Sovereignty Moonshot Plan to move India from being a consumer of frontier AI to becoming a stakeholder that helps shape its development, deployment, safety, and governance in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #AI #ArtificialIntelligence #DigitalInfrastructure #CyberSecurity #Innovation #EmergingTech #FrontierAI #ViksitBharat2047

On the occasion of National Technology Day, DRDO released three publications highlighting the organisation’s continued pursuit of technological innovation, scientific excellence and knowledge sharing in defence research & development. “Padma Awardees of DRDO” is a commemorative publication dedicated to distinguished DRDO personalities who have received the prestigious Padma Awards for their extraordinary contributions to science, technology, defence innovation and national service. “DRDO Technology Spectrum–2026” is an extensive compendium of futuristic technologies, pioneering research, transformative innovations and strategic scientific perspectives contributed by eminent scientists from various DRDO laboratories. The publication offers valuable insights into emerging technological domains shaping the future of national defence and strategic capabilities. “Raksha Anusandhan Bharti” is a thoughtfully compiled collection of Hindi articles centred on defence science, indigenous technologies, research achievements and scientific advancements, reflecting DRDO’s continuous efforts to promote scientific literature and technical communication in Hindi. The publications collectively reflect DRDO’s vision of fostering scientific temperament, strengthening indigenous technological capabilities and advancing India’s journey towards self-reliance in critical defence technologies. DRDO (@DRDO_India) On the occasion of National Technology Day 2026, DRDO’s Defence Science Forum and Scientific Analysis Group (SAG) organised a commemorative event at Dr S Bhagavantham Auditorium, Metcalfe House, Delhi. The programme was presided over by Dr B K Das, DS & DG (ECS) and featured addresses by Dr U K Singh and DS & DG (SSS), Chief Mentor DSF. The event was graced by Prof Manoj Singh Gaur, Director IIT Jammu, as Chief Guest and Sqn Ldr Sameer Joshi (Retd), CEO NewSpace Research & Technology as Guest of Honour, who delivered insightful keynote addresses on emerging technologies, innovation and self-reliance in the defence sector. The celebrations also included inspiring orations by scientists from DRDO laboratories, distribution of medals & certificates, and commendation to DRDO employees, along with the release of “DRDO Technology Spectrum-2026” and books including “Raksha Anusandhan Bharti” and “Padma Awardees of DRDO”. The event reflected DRDO’s continued commitment towards indigenous innovation, advanced research and strengthening India’s technological capabilities for national security. #NationalTechnologyDay #DRDO #Innovation #AatmanirbharBharat #DefenceTechnology #NTD2026 — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/DRDO_India/status/2053849640961966320#m

This website is like a piece of paper that's glued to the wall like you ripped it off of a magazine. There's panning and scrolling. The mental model of the page is vividly clear. Navigation is straightforward and predictable. Menu doesn't move. The 'staticness' of these old sites is undervalued and now kind of forgotten. Compare this with modern full screen webapps that give you no sense of where you are on the page and molasses-like animated UI that captures native scrolling. These websites have their own abstraction layer to navigate, browse and present things. Almost like motion picture that presents information to you and you don't have much control. Signifiers that visually inform you of interactability are misplaced or entirely missing. You have some illusion of control but it's nowhere as explicit as a static page. There is an ad-tech-smell and "pop" in modern websites as they take over your visual field in mysterious, unpredictable ways. Doesn't let go of the attention easily. Huge typography and motion effects captivate users kinda like a 30-sec advertisement. Crack cocaine of information consumption. Combine this with terrible decisions at the OS-level like making scrollbars invisible, practice of UI/UX is deeply unserious today. It's not like we don't have solutions and it's an unknown problem. We have the blueprints. We had it all and we deliberately abandoned it with great carelessness. But in a certain light, the practice of UI/UX today is deeply serious in the ad-tech aspects and bedazzles their userbase with ever-increasing sense of bedazzlement. What purpose does Apple Liquid Glass UI serve otherwise? Open for discussion and critique. Was Stonewall Jackson actually that good? Let me end this debate. In the spring of 1862, the Confederacy was losing. McClellan was marching 100,000 men up the Virginia Peninsula toward Richmond. The capital was about to fall. The war was about to end. Then a weird, lemon-sucking, ex-VMI physics professor changed everything. Thomas J. Jackson had 17,000 men in the Shenandoah Valley. The Union had three separate armies under Banks, Frémont, and Shields totaling over 60,000, all converging to crush him, then reinforce the assault on Richmond. What Jackson did next is still taught at West Point, Sandhurst, and the Israeli Defense Forces' command college. In 48 days, his "foot cavalry" marched 646 miles through the Blue Ridge. He fought five battles, McDowell, Front Royal, Winchester, Cross Keys, Port Republic, and won every single one. He used interior lines to appear in three places at once. He marched his men until their shoes fell off, then marched them more. He told no one his plans, not even his generals. When asked where he was going, he'd say "to do my duty." He didn't just defeat three armies. He paralyzed them. Lincoln personally diverted 40,000 reinforcements away from Richmond to chase a ghost. McClellan's offensive collapsed. Richmond was saved. He had done it with a third of the men. Then came Chancellorsville, May 1863. Lee was outnumbered 130,000 to 60,000 by Hooker's army. Most generals would've retreated. Lee split his army. Then Jackson split it AGAIN, taking 28,000 men on a 12-mile flank march directly across the front of a numerically superior enemy, a maneuver textbooks call suicidal. At dusk, his men exploded out of the woods into the unsuspecting Union right flank. The XI Corps disintegrated. It is, to this day, one of the most audacious tactical movements in the history of warfare. Hours later, riding ahead in the dark to plan a night attack, his own men shot him by mistake. His arm was amputated. He died of pneumonia eight days later. Lee, on hearing it: "He has lost his left arm, but I have lost my right." Patton studied him. Rommel studied him. Moshe Dayan reportedly modeled parts of the Six-Day War on his Valley Campaign. MacArthur called him the greatest natural military genius America ever produced. He was 39 years old. You can hate the cause. But pretending Jackson wasn't one of the most lethal field commanders in military history is just bad history. The man was a problem.

CBS News reports that, according to unnamed US officials, Iran moved several aircraft-including an Iranian Air Force RC-130 reconnaissance platform-to Pakistan’s Nur Khan Air Base near Rawalpindi shortly after the April ceasefire announcement. Personally, I have serious doubts about this report for several reasons. - Nur Khan is a highly important Pakistani military air base located near the country’s military and political nerve center in Rawalpindi. Allowing Iranian military aircraft, particularly an ISR platform, to openly operate or “park” there during a major regional crisis would represent an extraordinary step for Islamabad. - An RC-130 is not just a transport aircraft but an intelligence and reconnaissance platform, making the alleged deployment politically and strategically sensitive. - The report also appears difficult to reconcile with Pakistan’s broader balancing strategy during the crisis: maintaining channels with Tehran while simultaneously avoiding a direct rupture with Washington and Persian Gulf partners (i.e. KSA, which signed on September 2025 a mutual defense pact with Islamabad). This does not exclude quieter forms of coordination or temporary technical arrangements behind the scenes. But, from my point of view, the broader narrative presented in the report should be treated cautiously unless supported by stronger evidence. #Iran #Pakistan #US #Geopolitics

Today we held a high-level meeting of the International Coalition for the Return of Ukrainian Children, co-organized by Ukraine, Canada, and the EU. What Russia is doing to Ukrainian children is evil. This is not an accident of war. This is not collateral damage. This is a deliberate Russian policy aimed at destroying Ukrainian identity. Children are forced to forget who they are, where they come from, and even their own language. This is Russian social engineering. We saw this in the darkest past. And we know what horror it brings. The fact that this is happening is a verdict to international mechanisms that should have prevented such crimes. They failed. No other issue demonstrates it better than the issue of stolen Ukrainian children. Mechanisms need to be updated, new tools need to be invented, and enforcement needs to be real. We discussed this today. I am grateful to @KajaKallas, @AnitaAnnandMP, and @MartaKosGK for their dedication. I thank all partners who took part today and made concrete contributions. While our coalition has grown to 46 countries and 3 international organisations, we must transform this momentum into an effective mechanism that delivers measurable results—because statements alone are not enough to bring our children home. The fate of Ukrainian children will never be part of any compromise or "exchange list". Their freedom is unconditional, and Russia’s attempts to downplay this crime only prove their fear of justice. We are fighting for a triple return: return every child, return Ukraine to every child, and return childhood to every child. We must move toward concrete actions, including a strict Roadmap for coalition members and practical support for tracing and reintegration. We also call for the full implementation of the UNGA resolution and the enforcement of ICC arrest warrants against those responsible. Accountability is the only path to a lasting peace. Finally, there must be legal consequences for those involved in this evil, including so-called "adoptive families". I urge our partners to impose entry bans and tough sanctions on all Russians involved in the deportation and indoctrination of our children. Words of empathy are not enough; only political and legal actions will ensure these children finally come home.

Joint efforts remain essential to ensure the return of all Ukrainian children and to hold accountable those responsible for forced deportation, forced adoption, re-education, Russification, and militarisation of Ukrainian children. We are grateful to our partners for increasing pressure through sanctions. 🇬🇧 The United Kingdom has sanctioned 85 individuals and entities. 🇨🇦 Canada is imposing sanctions on 23 individuals and 5 organisations. 🇪🇺 The European Union sanctions target 16 individuals and 7 organisations. “These measures target not only individuals and entities, but also the entire machinery behind the forced deportation and assimilation of Ukrainian children. This is not politics. It is about protecting children, defending human dignity, and upholding international law,” stated Ukraine’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Andrii Sybiha.

China’s economic engine is stalling, and the global oil market is feeling the shockwaves. Crude oil imports plummeted 20% in April to just 8.2 million barrels per day, the lowest level in at least two years. This massive drop is equivalent to wiping out the entire daily oil consumption of Japan, signaling a deep and quiet contraction in domestic demand. While Beijing frames this as a strategic reshuffle, the data suggests a harder truth. Lower refinery runs and reduced buying from smaller refiners point to a significant slowdown in Chinese economic growth. By reselling crude cargoes to Europe and Asia, Chinese state companies are acting as an emergency buffer for a global supply shortage, but they are only able to do so because their own factories and transport networks are thirsting for less fuel. This demand destruction is the invisible hand currently capping global oil prices. As the CCP struggles with a cooling economy and the fallout from Middle East disruptions, its reduced appetite is the only thing preventing a total price explosion. For the world, it provides temporary relief from high costs. For the Party, it is a glaring admission that the industrial heart of China is beating much slower than they want the world to believe. #UnveiledChina #OilMarket #ChinaEconomy #EnergySecurity #DemandDestruction The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) China is quietly reshaping the global oil market: China's crude oil imports fell -20% MoM in April, to 8.2 million barrels per day, the lowest in at least 2 years. To put this into perspective, the decline nearly matches the daily total oil consumption of Japan. This is also 2 times larger than the volume supplied by the UAE pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Furthermore, Chinese state-owned oil companies have been reselling crude cargoes to European and Asian buyers, a sign that inventory levels are comfortable despite a global supply shortage. This is just heartbreaking. People are noticing Ella’s comments on SSRI addiction because she is well known, but there are millions upon millions like her. Who decided that it would be OK to medicate people once they hit puberty, when in all likelihood they would be on them for the rest of their lives? I first noticed it with the kids of the late-cohort boomers who were medicating their kids while Mrs. Salamander & I were just thinking of starting families of our own. It has only gotten worse in the three decades that followed. What would it be like to go through middle school, high school, and most of your 20s and then all of a sudden realize that you never really experienced reality…just what the drugs let you see, feel, endure? People have not changed. The Western Word has seen much more challenging circumstances for young people. These people did not make this decision. It was made for them, by the adults who in theory were supposed to have stewardship over their well being? It fits a pattern. I wish Ella the best in the process of trying, hopefully successfully, to get off these drugs. It cannot be easy. You have to, as an adult, get coping mechanisms that you could have had a decade+ to develop slowly over time. She did not ask for this. I give her great credit to, in a fashion, help raise the issue simply by asking questions…and for help. fireworks and confetti (@fworksconfetti) Ella Emhoff, stepdaughter of former Vice President Kamala Harris, from 16 December last year: "...I'm just sitting here crocheting, waiting for a friend, and I was just listening to this podcast that The Wall Street Journal put out about SSRIs and anti-anxiety meds and kind of the over-prescription of them in America. "And it was making me think a lot because I've been on SSRIs for over a decade, almost fifteen years probably, and they were calling out the lack of research on long-term use of these things. "They were calling out the lack of information that doctors give about coming off of these meds and kind of the psychological effects they can have. "And it really got me thinking how little I've thought about that, naively, obviously. "But I've noticed that every time I've gone off of it for a week or missed it or for whatever reason, like, it has been really hard for me, and I've had a really hard time. "And I guess this is just something I was wondering if you guys have thought about or relate to or kind of consider when you're thinking about going on meds like that. "Because I don't know if this is something that I feel like is being talked about enough because I feel like so many of us are on these meds, and this is, like, actually happening. "Like, people get off of them, and they kind of break down, and it can be really bad. So yeah, I guess I just want your general thoughts." I met Juliano online in 2008. We were competing at CodeGate CTF on different teams. Both of us failed a crypto challenge by @defendtheworld, but afterward we realized we were both obsessed with crypto and started talking. We were heavily inspired by @tqbf, @chriseng, Nate Lawson, and @cperciva, who were doing insanely cool work at the intersection of cryptography and web attacks. One thing led to another. We did the Flickr attack in 2009, then the padding oracle work in 2010. We finally met in person at Black Hat Europe 2010. Those years defined my career and my life too. 2010 especially felt like a turning point. We presented the ASP.NET attack at Ekoparty. The conference was inside a theater and the place was absolutely packed. People were literally lying on the floor. Everybody was chanting in Spanish. And to make things even more ridiculous, at the end of the talk we started throwing USB thumb drives with the PoC into the audience from the stage hahaha. At one point we were offered $20K for the exploit. My salary was $1,000/month, so this was more than 1 year of salary haha. But dropping it as a 0-day was much more fun and felt like a better deal. Not long after that, I got a job in the states at Matasano Security, and later ended up at Google. Juliano Rizzo (@julianor) The work I did with Thai @XorNinja starting with the hash extension against Flickr and later padding oracle research, was the most fun I've ever had doing security research. Over the years I've kept seeing new papers, advisories, and pentest stories using those ideas .. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/julianor/status/2053130341561315805#m

Lately I've been thinking about how AI is changing vulnerability research and reverse engineering. VR and RE are some of the hardest workflows to parallelize. Even with great knowledge transfer and team practices, you usually default to one person per vuln or RE task. The work is just too context-heavy to split. AI breaks that ceiling. It's no longer "one researcher, one task", it's you working one angle while Claude annotates disassembly code, explores another path, or helps you piece together what the last result means. Watching this land in domains we assumed were fundamentally serial is wild.

अश्लील इशारा करना पड़ा भारी, Tim David पर BCCI ने ठोका जुर्माना आरसीबी के स्टार खिलाड़ी टिम डेविड पर मुंबई इंडियंस के खिलाफ मैच जीतने के बाद अश्लील इशारा करने के लिए तगड़ा जुर्माना ठोका गया है. रविवार (10 मई) को रायपुर के शहीद वीर नारायण सिंह अंतर्राष्ट्रीय स्टेडियम में खेले गए रोमांचक मुकाबले में रॉयल चैलेंजर्स बेंगलुरु ने आखिरी गेंद पर जीत हासिल की. इसके बाद ड्रेसिंग रूम में जश्न का माहौल था, लेकिन खुशियों के बीच टिम डेविड ने शर्मनाक हरकत की, जिसकी क्लिप सोशल मीडिया पर आग की तरह फैल गई. आरसीबी की जीत के बाद उन्होंने उंगली दिखाते हुए अश्लील इशारा किया था. फैंस का मानना है कि उन्होंने ये इशारा मुंबई इंडियंस की ड्रेसिंग रूम की तरफ देखकर किया. बता दें कि टिम डेविड पहले मुंबई इंडियंस टीम का हिस्सा थे, लेकिन उन्हें बाहर का रास्ता दिखा दिया गया. क्रिकबज की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, रायपुर में एमआई के खिलाफ आरसीबी की जीत के दौरान आईपीएल आचार संहिता का उल्लंघन करने के लिए टिम डेविड पर उनकी मैच फीस का 30 प्रतिशत जुर्माना लगाया गया है और उन्हें 2 डिमेरिट पॉइंट दिए गए हैं. यह अपराध "अश्लील, आपत्तिजनक या अपमानजनक इशारे का इस्तेमाल" करने से संबंधित है. . . मुंबई इंडियंस के खिलाफ मैच में टिम डेविड बल्ले से पूरी तरह फ्लॉप हुए. वो बिना खाता खोले पवेलियन लौट गए थे. आरसीबी की जीत में ऑलराउंडर क्रुणाल पांड्या और भुवनेश्वर कुमार का अहम योगदान रहा. भुवी ने शानदार गेंदबाजी करते हुए मुंबई के 4 बल्लेबाजों को पवेलियन की राह दिखाई, जिसमें रोहित शर्मा और सूर्यकुमार यादव का विकेट शामिल है. उनके इस प्रदर्शन के दम पर आरसीबी ने मुंबई को 166 रनों पर रोक लिया. लक्ष्य का पीछा करते हुए RCB ने 39 रन पर कोहली, पडिक्कल और पाटीदार के प्रमुख विकेट खो दिए थे. क्रुणाल पांड्या ने अपने कंधों पर जिम्मेदारी ली और संकटमोचक बने. उन्होंने 73 रनों की कीमती पारी खेली. आखिरी में भुवनेश्वर कुमार ने छक्का लगाकर टीम को जीत दिलाई. इस जीत के बाद रॉयल चैलेंजर्स बेंगलुरु पॉइंट्स टेबल पर पहले स्थान पर पहुंच गई है. #TimDavid #RCB #BCCI #IPL #IPL2026

Hamas leaders are currently meeting in Istanbul to finalize the selection of the new leader of the Political Bureau, which is expected to be announced in the coming days. Hamas sources outside Gaza say that Khalil Al-Hayya, Hamas leader in Gaza, will likely be named Hamas's new leader, according to Saudi A-Sharq Al-Awsat. Some of the sources stated that Al-Hayya is expected to receive the appointment, especially after the elimination of his fourth son by Israel last week. "It is not unlikely that voters will give Al-Hayya the most votes in appreciation of his sacrifices," the sources said. Al-Hayya is set to return to Istanbul either tonight or tomorrow morning "to resume his duties," including finalizing preparations for the election of the new political bureau chief. For the past year and a half, Hamas had no political bureau chief, following the elimination of Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran in July, 2024. It was managed by a "leadership council" instead. The newly selected political bureau chief will hold the position until the end of 2026, as Hamas awaits "suitable security and political conditions to hold comprehensive elections in all regions, to select a new Shura Council, political bureau, and executive body, as well as at the regional, district, and local levels." Meanwhile, the Hamas delegation is set to hold meetings with mediators from Egypt, Qatar and Turkey in Istanbul in the coming days. According to a source from the Palestinian factions, the mediators, especially Egypt, will present a new proposal to end the deadlock in negotiations over further implementing Trump's 20-point plan for Gaza. According to A-Sharq Al-Awsat, the Peace Council's high Representative to Gaza, Nikolay Mladenov, conveyed to Hamas Israel's conditions regarding disarmament, as well as its refusal to link withdrawal from Gaza with reconstruction.

On August 1, 1960, President Dwight D. Eisenhower received a letter from a frustrated citizen named Leon Scott. Mr. Scott asked Eisenhower why he had a picture of Robert E. Lee in his office. This was Eisenhower's response to Mr. Scott: "Dear Dr. Scott, Respecting your August 1 inquiry calling attention to my often expressed admiration for General Robert E. Lee, I would say, first, that we need to understand that at the time of the War between the States, the issue of secession had remained unresolved for more than 70 years. Men of probity, character, public standing, and unquestioned loyalty, both North and South, had disagreed over this issue as a matter of principle from the day our Constitution was adopted. General Robert E. Lee was, in my estimation, one of the supremely gifted men produced by our Nation. He believed unswervingly in the Constitutional validity of his cause which, until 1865, was still an arguable question in America; he was a poised and inspiring leader, true to the high trust reposed in him by millions of his fellow citizens; he was thoughtful yet demanding of his officers and men, forbearing with captured enemies but ingenious, unrelenting, and personally courageous in battle, and never disheartened by a reverse or obstacle. Through all his many trials, he remained selfless almost to a fault and unfailing in his faith in God. Taken altogether, he was noble as a leader and as a man, and unsullied as read the pages of our history. From deep conviction, I simply say this: a nation of men of Lee's calibre would be unconquerable in spirit and soul. Indeed, to the degree that present-day American youth will strive to emulate his rare qualities, including his devotion to this land as revealed in his painstaking efforts to help heal the Nation's wounds once the bitter struggle was over, we, in our own time of danger in a divided world, will be strengthened and our love of freedom sustained. Such are the reasons that I proudly display the picture of this great American on my office wall. Sincerely, Dwight D. Eisenhower"

You might be cool, but you’ll never be Erik Bonde… a Swedish Major fighting during the Congo Crisis smoking a cigarette after being shot in an ambush while rocking a Lemania TG 195 type of cool. Born in Sweden to gentry (nobility), he inherited the title of “Count.” He started off in the Swedish Army, in the cavalry. He got out in order to persue a life of agriculture but was recalled and reinstated in order to take command of the first Swedish Battalion in Katanga. This timeless photo was taken immediately following an ambush on his elements in which MAJ Bonde was shot multiple times by inferior hostile weapons (mostly outdated muzzle loaders). After the firefight, one of his soldiers ran up and remarked “Sir! You are hit! Your shirt is red!” Bonde shook his head, sighed, took off his shirt, lit a smoke, and looked at him. “Don’t be impertinent. I’m a Count. My blood is blue.” The man makes the watch. If social media posts of Judge Hamayoun Dilawar are authentic (Tosha Khana Case Judge), this is alarming and raises serious and reasonable doubts on credibility of trial being conducted by him. In my view, propriety demands that he should immediately recuse or disassociate himself from the case. It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. Court further held that bias is mental disposition or attitude towards a particular person and covers all kind of hostilities and prejudices against him.

🌐 Strengthening regional collaboration on transfer pricing and tax administration. On 29–30 April, the third virtual workshop under the Caribbean Tax Outreach Programme brought together 225 government officials from 18 jurisdictions to examine transfer pricing rules and their growing relevance across the Caribbean region. Co-hosted by the OECD, CARICOM, CATA, CIAT, IMF CARTAC and the World Bank Group, the two-day workshop explored key policy and administrative approaches, transfer pricing methodologies, intra-group services, and practical experiences from participating countries. 💡 Highlights included: ▪️ Tax Administration Jamaica (TAJ) sharing its decade-long journey in strengthening Jamaica’s transfer pricing framework; ▪️ The Dominican Republic (DGII) outlining its evolving framework and the implementation of Advance Pricing Arrangements (APAs) in the hospitality sector; ▪️ Maldives Inland Revenue Authority (MIRA Maldives) showcasing the support provided through Tax Inspectors Without Borders (TIWB) to address tourism sector transfer pricing risks; and ▪️ Discussions on “Amount B” and its potential relevance for low-capacity jurisdictions. The workshop series continues to support experience sharing, capacity building and the advancement of key tax priorities across the Caribbean Community. #CARICOM #TaxCooperation #RegionalDevelopment #Caribbean #TaxAdministration #OECD #CapacityBuilding

The Speaker of the National Assembly, Thoko Didiza, has outlined the steps Parliament will take following a landmark Constitutional Court judgment that declared parts of the National Assembly’s impeachment rules unconstitutional and ordered the revival of the Section 89 process linked to the Independent Panel report chaired by former Chief Justice Sandile Ngcobo. In a statement issued on Monday, Parliament confirmed that it would comply fully with the Constitutional Court ruling delivered on Friday in the matter of Economic Freedom Fighters and Another v Speaker of the National Assembly and Others. The apex court found Rule 129I of the Rules of the National Assembly unconstitutional and invalid, setting the rule aside. The court also ordered an interim amendment, known as a “reading-in” to govern the handling of Section 89 impeachment matters until Parliament formally amends its rules. The ruling further invalidated the National Assembly’s decision of 13 December 2022 not to refer the Independent Panel report to an impeachment committee. The Constitutional Court ordered that the report now be sent to an Impeachment Committee established under the Assembly’s rules. tinyurl.com/3acn8zdc #GovZAUpdates

اسلام آباد : 11 مئی، 2026. وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے ملکی برآمدات میں اضافے کے حوالے سے حکمت عملی پر اجلاس کی صدارت کی. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ برآمدات پر مبنی صنعت، ملکی ترقی کے اہداف کے حصول کے لئے نا گزیر ہے. حکومت اپنی توجہ برآمدات میں اضافے اور صنعتوں کو سہولیات فراہم کرنے ہر مزکور کئے ہوئے ہے. وزیرِ اعظم نے ہدایت کی کہ ایسےچھوٹے اور درمیانے درجے کے کاروبار اور صنعتیں، جو کہ برآمدات میں اضافے کے حوالے سے اہم ہیں، کو حکومتی سہولیات فراہم کرنے کے حوالےسے لائحہ عمل تیار کیا جائے. ایسے نئے کاروباروں اور صنعتوں کے فروغ کے لیے بھی حکمت عملی مرتب کی جائے جو ملکی برآمدات میں اضافے کا باعث بنیں. وزیرِ اعظم نے اپنی گفتگو کے دوران مزید کہا کہ ملکی صنعت اور تجارت میں ریسرچ اینڈ ڈویلپمنٹ اور جدت, ملکی مصنوعات کو عالمی مارکیٹ میں مسابقت دلانے میں مددگار ثابت ہو گی. وزیر اعظم نے برآمد کنندگان کو ٹیکس ریفنڈ کی بروقت ادئیگی کی بھی ہدایت کی. اجلاس کو ملکی برآمدات میں اضافے کے حوالے سے حکمت عملی پر بریفنگ دی گئی ؛ پالیسی مسودے پر اجلاس میں تفصیلی گفتگو و تبادلہ خیال بھی کیا گیا اور شرکاء نے اپنی اپنی آراء اور تجاویز پیش کیں. اجلاس میں نائب وزیراعظم و وزیر خارجہ اسحاق ڈار ، وفاقی وزیر اقتصادی امور احد خان چیمہ ، وفاقی وزیر تجارت جام کمال خان ، وفاقی وزیر قومی غذائی تحفظ و تحقیق رانا تنویر حسین ، وفاقی وزیر موسمیاتی تبدیلی ڈاکٹر مصدق ملک ، وفاقی وزیر خزانہ و محصولات محمد اورنگزیب ، وفاقی وزیر انفارمیشن ٹیکنالوجی و ٹیلی کام شزہ فاطمہ خواجہ ،وزیر مملکت برائے خزانہ و ریلوے بلال اظہر کیانی ، وزیراعظم کے معا ون خصوصی برائے صنعت و پیداوار ہارون اختر اور متعلقہ اعلیٰ سرکاری افسران نے شرکت کی ۔ Video

Deputy Prime Minister / Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 spoke today with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud @FaisalbinFarhan on the evolving regional situation and matters of mutual interest. The Saudi Foreign Minister appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and reiterated support for Islamabad’s efforts aimed at promoting regional peace and stability, particularly in the context of ongoing engagement between Iran and the United States. On the occasion of National Technology Day 2026, DRDO’s Defence Science Forum and Scientific Analysis Group (SAG) organised a commemorative event at Dr S Bhagavantham Auditorium, Metcalfe House, Delhi. The programme was presided over by Dr B K Das, DS & DG (ECS) and featured addresses by Dr U K Singh and DS & DG (SSS), Chief Mentor DSF. The event was graced by Prof Manoj Singh Gaur, Director IIT Jammu, as Chief Guest and Sqn Ldr Sameer Joshi (Retd), CEO NewSpace Research & Technology as Guest of Honour, who delivered insightful keynote addresses on emerging technologies, innovation and self-reliance in the defence sector. The celebrations also included inspiring orations by scientists from DRDO laboratories, distribution of medals & certificates, and commendation to DRDO employees, along with the release of “DRDO Technology Spectrum-2026” and books including “Raksha Anusandhan Bharti” and “Padma Awardees of DRDO”. The event reflected DRDO’s continued commitment towards indigenous innovation, advanced research and strengthening India’s technological capabilities for national security. #NationalTechnologyDay #DRDO #Innovation #AatmanirbharBharat #DefenceTechnology #NTD2026

करोड़ों युवा रातें जागकर पढ़ते हैं, परिवार अपना सब कुछ दांव पर लगाता है। लेकिन सत्ता की छत्रछाया में पल रहे पेपर लीक माफिया मिनटों में उनकी सालों की मेहनत बेच देते हैं। पेपर लीक सिर्फ भ्रष्टाचार नहीं, युवाओं के सपनों की हत्या है। जो नेता इन माफियाओं को बचा रहे हैं, वे देश के मेहनती युवाओं के भविष्य के अपराधी हैं। आज सिस्टम इतना सड़ चुका है कि परीक्षा से पहले ही प्रश्नपत्र बाजार में बिक जाते हैं। मेहनत करने वाला छात्र ठगा जाता है और पैसे व पहुंच वाले लोग आगे निकल जाते हैं। भाजपा सरकार कैमरों के सामने कार्रवाई का नाटक करती हैं, लेकिन असली गुनहगार उन्ही के राजनीतिक संरक्षण में खुले घूमते हैं। अगर अब भी युवा नहीं उठे, तो डिग्रियां, नौकरियां और भविष्य सब बिकाऊ हो जाएंगे। अब लड़ाई सिर्फ एक परीक्षा की नहीं, पूरे सिस्टम को बदलने की है। ASHUTOSH MISHRA (@JournoAshutosh) NEET 2026 परीक्षा फिर सवालों के घेरे में। राजस्थान पुलिस की जाँच में बड़ा ख़ुलासा, केरल से सीकर पहुँचा गेस पेपर जिसमें १४० सवाल परीक्षा पेपर से हूबहू मिले। 720 अंकों में से 600 अंकों के सवाल मिले, पुलिस ने कई लोगों को हिरासत में लिया गया। ५ लाख रुपए में गेस पेपर बेचे गए।अब NTA को तय करना है कि परीक्षा दोबारा होगी या नहीं। — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/JournoAshutosh/status/2053679660085686696#m

Wayanad’s long-cherished dream is moving closer to reality. On March 6, the first blasting will be switched on at Anakkampoyil, marking the start of rock excavation for the Anakkampoyil–Kalladi–Meppadi tunnel road. Implemented through KIIFB at a cost of ₹2143 crore, this 8.735 km four-lane tunnel will transform connectivity and open new possibilities for the economic, agricultural, tourism and healthcare sectors of the Malabar region. Once considered impossible, such major infrastructure is now becoming reality through careful planning and political will. This is another firm step in building a New Kerala committed to comprehensive and people-centred development.

🇷🇺⚔️🇺🇦Russian Defense Ministry on progress of special military operation 11 May 2026 ❗️ In accordance with the decision of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation, during the holidays on the occasion of the 81st anniversary of the Great Victory, all groups of the Russian troops in the special military operation zone continue to strictly observe the ceasefire since 00:00 of 8 May remaining in previously taken positions. ▪️ Despite the announcement of a ceasefire regime, the Ukrainian armed formations carried out strikes using unmanned aerial vehicles and conducted artillery fire against the Russian positions. ▪️ Over the past day, the Armed Forces of Ukraine have made 12 attempts to launch attacks and have carried out 767 strikes against Russian troops using MLRSs, artillery guns, and mortars. They delivered 6,905 strikes using unmanned aerial vehicles. ▪️ In total, 23,802 ceasefire violations by the Ukrainian side were recorded during the ceasefire period in the special military operation zone. ▪️ Moreover, the enemy delivered strikes at civilian facilities in Belgorod region, using 18 UAVs, including eight fixed-wing ones and 10 copters. Two local residents were wounded. Three motor vehicles, one store building, one apartment building, and two private houses were damaged. ▫️ The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation have mirrored the actions of the AFU. Retaliatory fire was carried out on MLRS positions, artillery, and mortar positions. Command and control posts and launch points of unmanned aerial vehicles were engaged. In response to the enemy's fire attacks, units of the Sever Group of Forces hit manpower and hardware of the AFU mechanized brigade near Zapselye (Sumy region). In Kharkov region, units of two mechanized brigades of the AFU and one territorial defense brigade were neutralized by fire close to Ryasnoye, Shesterovka, and Budarki (Kharkov region). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to up to 90 troops, five motor vehicles, and two field artillery guns. In the course of the retaliatory strikes, units of the Zapad Group of Forces hit formations of two mechanized brigades of the AFU close to Krestishche and Mayaki (Donetsk People's Republic). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to more than 90 troops, two armored fighting vehicles, 20 motor vehicles, and three artillery guns, including two Western-made ones. The Yuzhnaya Group's units repelled three attacks launched by assault groups of two mechanized brigades and one mountain assault brigade of the AFU near Konstantinovka, Khimik, Artema and Ray-Aleksandrovka (Donetsk People's Republic). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to over 70 troops, six armored fighting vehicles, 15 motor vehicles, and two artillery guns. The Tsentr Group of Forces repelled nine attacks launched by AFU assault groups and hit by retaliatory fire manpower and hardware of two mechanized brigades, one airmobile brigade, one assault regiment of the AFU, and one marine brigade close to Novoleksandrovka, Kucherov Yar, Lenina, Belitskoye, (Donetsk People's Republic), Novopavlovka, and Novopodgorodnoye (Dnepropetrovsk region). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to more than 305 troops, six armored fighting vehicles, 13 motor vehicles, and two artillery guns. In response to the enemy's fire attacks, units of the Vostok Group of Forces inflicted fire damage on formations of one air assault brigade, two assault brigades, and two assault regiments of the AFU close to Verkhnaya Tersa, Charivnoye, and Vozdvizhevka (Zaporozhye region). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to more than 320 troops, one armored fighting vehicle, and four motor vehicles. The Dnepr Group of Forces inflicted losses on manpower and hardware of one mechanized brigade and one mountain assault brigade of the AFU close to Preobrazhenka and Zaporozhets (Zaporozhye region). ▪️ Up to 45 troops, 17 motor vehicles, and one artillery gun were neutralized. Operational-Tactical Aviation, attack drones, and missile troops of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation didn't deliver strikes. ▫️ Air defense systems shot down 85 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles. In total, since the beginning of the special military operation, the enemy has lost: - 671 aircraft, - 284 helicopters, - 144,888 unmanned aerial vehicles, - 661 anti-aircraft missile systems, - 29,260 tanks and other armored fighting vehicles, - 1,718 MLRS combat vehicles, - 34,864 field artillery guns and mortars, - 61,323 special military vehicles. We continue our nearly daily communication with representatives of the United States. Today, Rustem Umerov briefed me on the outcomes of his meetings with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Importantly, America remains engaged in diplomacy and, in particular, has acted as a mediator on the issue of a prisoner exchange. Contacts are ongoing at the appropriate level to hammer out the configuration of the exchange. The lists have been handed over, and we expect the American side to play an active role in ensuring the realization of this agreement. Possible formats for meetings and negotiations at the leadership level aimed at ending Russia’s war were also discussed in the United States. Rustem also provided a separate detailed report on contacts with countries interested in Drone Deals with Ukraine. Nearly 20 countries are currently involved at various stages: 4 agreements have already been signed, and the first contracts under these agreements are now being prepared. With other countries, preparatory procedures are underway for political arrangements that will open the way for businesses. Ukraine has already secured its first energy-related results thanks to these agreements – the Ukrainian market is being supplied with the necessary volume of fuel. There will also be significant financial results. In addition to the Middle East and the Gulf, the South Caucasus, and Europe, we will soon launch this new security cooperation within the framework of Drone Deals with another part of the world as well. We are preparing positive news for Ukraine. Glory to Ukraine!

The modernisation and expansion of the United Nations Office at Nairobi is a powerful expression of inclusivity, geographical balance and the universality of the United Nations system. To complement the modernisation of the UN campus, we are investing $1.1 billion in complementary support for Nairobi’s infrastructure upgrade, including roads, street lighting, regeneration of the Nairobi Rivers, ICT systems security, and the operationalisation of the UN One-Stop Shop. This investment affirms Nairobi’s role as the UN’s headquarters in the Global South, a centre of international diplomacy, and a symbol of international cooperation. Additionally, we are modernising the Bomas Convention Complex to strengthen Kenya’s position as a hub for international conferencing.

Broke ground for the construction of the expanded United Nations Office at Nairobi Assembly Hall, Gigiri, and inaugurated the new United Nations Office block alongside UN Secretary-General @antonioguterres.

We are a country where the Inspector General of Police appears unaware that law enforcement cannot raid or attack buildings without a proper warrant. Where the Planning Minister and Finance Minister rarely sit together, compare notes, or align their strategies. Where The Finance Minister openly states that the IMF essentially writes his budget and that he must seek permission for major decisions. Meanwhile, the Planning Minister offers no credible growth strategy—only ad-hoc, foundationless policies that lack vision or substance. Too many ministries operate without clear purpose or competence. The Education Ministry, for instance, busies itself with interfering in autonomous institutions, restricting their ability to actually teach rather than enabling excellence. Parliament routinely passes laws without reading them, without meaningful debate, and without addressing the serious challenges confronting the nation. Academia produces little genuine research and offers almost no practical ideas or solutions to the country’s pressing problems. Civil society remains largely disengaged—focused primarily on weddings, funerals, and performative roles as speakers and audiences at donor-funded conferences that generate more talk than impact. Foreign lenders and consultants routinely shape policy to suit their own priorities rather than the needs and aspirations of the country’s people. And the judiciary frequently (but after decades of deliberation) undermines contracts and economic value through rulings that show little regard for economic analysis or a coherent understanding of law and economics. This is a system marked by fragmentation, lack of accountability, and institutional drift—where form often replaces function, and short-term expediency crowds out long-term national interest.

महाराष्ट्र परिवर्तनाचा भाग नव्हे, परिवर्तनाचे नेतृत्व करणारे राज्य! मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी आज नवी दिल्ली येथे 'CII ॲन्युअल बिझनेस समिट 2026' येथे सीआयआयचे महासंचालक चंद्रजीत बॅनर्जी आणि सीआयआयचे अध्यक्ष राजीव मेमानी यांच्यासमवेत 'व्हिजन फॉर इंडिया@ 100' या विषयावर संवाद साधला. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस म्हणाले, बऱ्याचदा असे क्षण येतात, जेव्हा एखादा देश केवळ बदलाचा भाग राहत नाही, तर स्वतः परिवर्तनाचा मार्ग दाखवतो. आज भारत अशाच निर्णायक टप्प्यावर उभा असून जगाला नवी दिशा देत आहे. जगभरात अनिश्चिततेचे वातावरण असताना भारत जागतिक स्तरावर भक्कमपणे उभा आहे. पंतप्रधान नरेंद्र मोदी यांच्या दूरदर्शी नेतृत्वामुळे गेल्या 10 वर्षांत जगाचा भारताकडे पाहण्याचा दृष्टिकोन पूर्णपणे बदलला असून, स्थिर धोरणे, मोठी स्वप्ने आणि प्रभावी कामगिरीमुळे आज भारताला जागतिक स्तरावर नवी ओळख मिळाली आहे, असे प्रतिपादन मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी केले. 'The Viksit Bharat Abhiyan-India @ 100' हे 2047 पर्यंत भारताला विकसित राष्ट्र बनवण्याचे महत्त्वाकांक्षी ध्येय आहे. हे ध्येय साध्य करण्यात राज्यांची भूमिका अत्यंत महत्त्वाची आहे. वेगवान विकास, व्यापक प्रगती आणि परिवर्तनशील दृष्टिकोनाच्या जोरावर महाराष्ट्र या प्रवासात आघाडीवर राहील, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस म्हणाले, महाराष्ट्रात देशातील सर्वात मोठी जीसीसी परिसंस्था विकसित झाली असून देशातील सुमारे 24% जीसीसी परिसंस्था एकट्या महाराष्ट्रात आहे. तसेच, महाराष्ट्र आशियातील सर्वात महत्त्वाच्या डेटा इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर कॉरिडोरपैकी एक म्हणून उदयास येत आहे. एआय, सेमीकंडक्टर्स, ईव्ही, स्वच्छ ऊर्जा, डेटा सेंटर्स, जीसीसी आणि डीप-टेक हे भविष्यातील अर्थव्यवस्थेची दिशा ठरवणार असून महाराष्ट्र या परिवर्तनाच्या केंद्रस्थानी उभा राहत आहे. भविष्यातील उद्योग अशा ठिकाणांना प्राधान्य देतील, जिथे हरित ऊर्जा, उत्कृष्ट पायाभूत सुविधा, सक्षम पुरवठा साखळी आणि पर्यावरणपूरक विकासाला चालना मिळेल. महाराष्ट्रातही अशाच प्रकारची जागतिक दर्जाची व्यवस्था उभारली जात असून, येथे स्थिर धोरणे, जलद निर्णयप्रक्रिया आणि विश्वासार्ह अंमलबजावणी सुनिश्चित केली जात असल्याचे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी नमूद केले. @narendramodi @Dev_Fadnavis @CB_CII @rajivmemani @FollowCII #NewDelhi #DevendraFadnavis #CIIAnnualBusinessSummit26

وزارت خارجه‌ی پاکستان در واکنش به حمله بر یک پاسگاه پولیس در ولسوالی بنو ایالت خیبرپختونخوا، سرداراحمد شکیب، کاردار سفارت طالبان در اسلام‌آباد را احضار و مراتب اعتراض شدید پاکستان را ابلاغ کرده است. این وزارت امروز (دوشنبه، ۲۱ ثور) با نشر اعلامیه‌ای گفته است: «تحقیقات مفصل درباره‌ی این حمله، همراه با شواهد جمع‌آوری‌شده و اطلاعات تخنیکی، نشان می‌دهد که این حمله توسط تروریست‌های مستقر در افغانستان طراحی و هدایت شده است.» پاسگاه «فتح‌خیل» در ولسوالی بنو ایالت خیبرپختونخوا پاکستان شنبه‌شب هدف حمله‌ی انتحاری و مسلحانه قرار گرفت و در آن دست‌کم ۱۵ سرباز پولیس کشته و چهار نفر دیگر، شامل یک غیرنظامی، زخمی شدند. بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/253398

اسماعیل بقایی، سخن‌گوی وزارت خارجه‌ی ایران می‌گوید که این کشور در پاسخ خود به پیشنهاد امریکا، خواستان پایان جنگ در منطقه، به‌شمول لبنان، توقف «راهزنی دریایی» و آزادسازی دارایی‌های مسدودشده‌ی مردم ایران شده است. سخن‌گوی وزارت خارجه‌ی ایران امروز (دوشنبه، ۲۱ ثور) در یک نشست خبری گفت: «هرآنچه ما پیشنهاد کردیم، خواسته‌های معقول، مسئولانه و پیشنهادهای سخاوتمندانه بوده است؛ نه فقط برای منافع ملی ایران، بلکه برای خیر و ثبات و امنیت کل منطقه و جهان.» او گفت که اقدامات امریکا و اسرائیل پس از آغاز جنگ با ایران، «موجب اخلال در آزادی دریانوردی شده و در آب‌های آزاد به کشتی‌های ایرانی تعرض صورت گرفته است. همه‌ی این موارد قرار بود که در چارچوب این بسته‌ی پیشنهادی مورد بحث و تصمیم‌گیری قرار بگیرد». بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/253394

اسلام آباد : 11 مئی، 2026 وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے وزارت انفارمیشن ٹیکنالوجی و ٹیلی کام کے امور پر جائزہ اجلاس کی صدارت کی. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ ملک میں آئی ٹی کے شعبے کا فروغ اور آئی ٹی سے متعلق برآمدات میں اضافہ حکومت کی اولین ترجیحات میں شامل ہے. پاکستان کے نوجوانوں میں آئی ٹی کے حوالے سے بے پناہ استعداد موجود ہے جس سے بھرپور استفادہ حاصل کیا جانا چاہئیے. وزیراعظم نے ہدایت کی کہ گلگت بلتستان اور آزاد جموں و کشمیر میں آسان خدمت مراکز کے قیام کے حوالےسے کام تیز کیا جائے. آسان خدمت کی سہولیات کو صوبوں میں بھی شروع کرنے کے حوالےسے صوبائی حکومتوں کے ساتھ مل کر کام کیا جائے. آئی ٹی کے شعبے میں شہری اور دیہی علاقوں کے درمیان فرق کو کم کرنے کے لئے صوبائی و ڈسٹرکٹ کی سطح پر حکومتوں کا تعاون حاصل کیا جائے۔ اجلاس کو ملک میں آئی ٹی کے فروغ کے حوالے سے اقدامات پر بریفنگ دی گئی. بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ ملک بھر میں گھریلو انٹرنیٹ کنکشنز کی تعداد 2024 میں 1.9 ملین سے بڑھ کر 2026 میں 5.10 ملین ہوگئی ہے۔ رواں مالی سال پاکستان سے 4.5 سے 4.6 بلین امریکی ڈالرز کی آئی ٹی برآمدات متوقع ہیں. بریفنگ میں مزید بتایا گیا کہ حال ہی میں پاکستان میں 5 جی سروسز کے لئے نیلامی کی گئی جو کہ اس حوالے سے 2016 سے اب تک ہونے والی دنیا کی سب سے بڑی نیلامی تھی؛ اس آکشن سے پاکستان کو 509 ملین امریکی ڈالرز کا ریونیو حاصل ہوا. مصنوعی ذہانت کے فروغ کے حوالے سےفروری 2025 میں انڈس اے آئی ویک کا اہتمام کیا گیا ؛ 30 شہروں میں تقریبات ہوئیں. انڈس اے آئی ویک میں 100 سے زائد بین الاقوامی مندوبین نے شرکت کی ؛ 88 پویلیئنز بنائے گئے. اسلام آباد کے سرکاری اسکولوں اور ہیلتھ یونٹس کو فائبر کنیکٹیویٹی فراہم کر دی گئی ہے. اجلاس کو بتایا گیا کہ اسلام آباد کو فری انٹرنیٹ ہاٹ اسپاٹس کی فراہمی کا کام حتمی مرحلے میں ہے. سید پور ماڈل ویلج اور فاطمہ جناح پارک میں ای-لرننگ پاڈز (E-learning pods) نصب کئے جا رہے ہیں. اجلاس میں وفاقی وزیر منصوبہ بندی احسن اقبال ، وفاقی وزیر قانون و انصاف اعظم نذیر تارڑ ، وفاقی وزیر اقتصادی امور احد خان چیمہ ، وفاقی وزیر انفارمیشن ٹیکنالوجی و ٹیلی کام شزہ فاطمہ خواجہ ، وزیر مملکت برائے خزانہ و ریلوے بلال اظہر کیانی اور متعلقہ اعلیٰ سرکاری افسران نے شرکت کی ۔ Video

India and Pakistan have long been strategic rivals, but their military doctrines differ sharply. Pakistan traditionally follows a policy of strategic ambiguity — revealing only enough military capability to deter adversaries while keeping its full capabilities uncertain. India, by contrast, increasingly projects an image of power that often exceeds its demonstrated capabilities. The recent controversy surrounding the alleged test of the Agni-6 intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) reflects this divergence. Large sections of the Indian media, amplified by political messaging from the ruling Narendra Modi government and the Bharatiya Janata Party, celebrated the missile launch as a historic breakthrough. Reports claimed India had tested a 10,000-kilometre-range nuclear-capable ICBM capable of striking anywhere in the world. BJP social media campaigns even declared that India was entering the league of global superpowers. Yet the available evidence tells a different story. The Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) issued before the launch restricted airspace over a corridor of roughly 3,560 kilometres — significantly below the range associated with a true ICBM and even lower than the publicly discussed capabilities of the Agni-5 system. Several respected Indian defence commentators, including Shekhar Gupta and Snehesh Alex Philip, criticised the exaggerated claims, warning that hyper-nationalist “chest-thumping” damages India’s credibility internationally. More importantly, the timing and location of the test suggest political signalling rather than technological transformation. Conducted shortly after the BJP’s political gains in West Bengal and launched from the Odisha coast, the missile was reportedly visible from parts of Bangladesh, including Dhaka and Chattogram. This has led to speculation that the test was designed not only to signal strength toward Pakistan and China, but also to send a symbolic message to Bangladesh amid changing regional politics and the rise of Hindutva-driven nationalism in eastern India. #IndiaOut Ultimately, the controversy reveals how defence achievements in South Asia are increasingly intertwined with domestic politics, media sensationalism, and regional psychological signalling.

सोमनाथ पुनर्निर्माण के 75 गौरवशाली वर्ष पूर्ण होने के पावन अवसर पर आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री @narendramodi जी की गरिमामयी उपस्थिति में आज सम्पूर्ण राष्ट्र “सोमनाथ स्वाभिमान पर्व” मना रहा है। इस ऐतिहासिक अवसर पर आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी ने श्री सोमनाथ मंदिर में पूर्ण विधि-विधान के साथ पूजा-अर्चना एवं जलाभिषेक किया। यह केवल एक मंदिर के पुनर्निर्माण की यात्रा नहीं, बल्कि भारत की सनातन चेतना, सांस्कृतिक स्वाभिमान और राष्ट्रीय आत्मगौरव के पुनर्जागरण का अमर प्रतीक है। इस ऐतिहासिक अवसर के लाइव प्रसारण में सम्मिलित हुई और चांदनी चौक स्थित प्राचीन गौरी शंकर मंदिर में पूजा-अर्चना एवं जलाभिषेक कर देवाधिदेव महादेव से समस्त देशवासियों के सुख, समृद्धि और कल्याण की प्रार्थना की। सोमनाथ केवल एक मंदिर नहीं, बल्कि भारत की अखंड आस्था और आध्यात्मिक शक्ति का प्रतीक है। अनगिनत आक्रमणों और विध्वंसों के बाद भी सोमनाथ का पुनर्निर्माण यह संदेश देता है कि भारत की संस्कृति, श्रद्धा और सनातन चेतना शाश्वत है। आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी के नेतृत्व में आज भारत “विकास भी, विरासत भी” के मंत्र के साथ अपनी सांस्कृतिक पहचान को नए वैभव के साथ पुनर्प्रतिष्ठित कर रहा है। काशी विश्वनाथ से केदारनाथ और महाकाल लोक से सोमनाथ तक, यह कालखंड भारत की सांस्कृतिक चेतना के पुनर्जागरण का साक्षी बन रहा है। इस अवसर पर कैबिनेट सहयोगी श्री प्रवेश साहिब सिंह जी, श्री मनजिंदर सिंह सिरसा जी, श्री कपिल मिश्रा जी सहित बड़ी संख्या में श्रद्धालु उपस्थित रहे। हर हर महादेव जय सोमनाथ @p_sahibsingh @mssirsa @KapilMishra_IND #SomnathVirasatK75Varsh

The main ukrainian 🇺🇦 challenge for the next few months is to counter the massive air guided bombs (KAB) campaign. On the hottest area of the frontline (Hulialpole, Dobropilla and Sloviansk), Russia is constantly hitting everything with KABs. In total, I mapped 6 600 impacts for the last ~3 months on this 150 km long frontline. ▫️Near Hulialpole, I mapped around 1 687 FAB guided bombs impacts. The precision of those is around 80 to 90% hitting something (treelines, position, urban area). This is where the strike campaign is the most worrying, with an excellent precision and a high concentration of hits. ▫️On the Novopavlivka-Pokrovsk'e front, I mapped around 559 airstrikes impacts, which are much less numerous, focused on strongholds with a much lower precision (~20%). This is not an organized campaign but an usual use of these bombs. ▫️On the Pokrovsk-Dobropilla frontline (which extends to Kostiantynivka), I mapped around 3 500 FAB impacts, with most of them on the Dobropilla area. This is a real strike campaign but the precision is much less the case here, with around 20/30% hitting something and the remaining ones falling on the fields. ▫️Finally, the last studies area is the SLoviansk one. Here too, we can see a recent surge in strikes, with high concentration on key forests around the strategic village of Rai Oleksandrivka. Here, I counted ~820 impacts with a higher precision (~60%) since most are hitting forests. One thing to keep in mind is the number of monthly strikes. We have around 6 690 strikes reported for April in Ukraine and I mapped around 37% of those. Another interesting point is the fact that it's more difficult to find strikes impacts in cities, that's why you have less dots on Kostiantynivka, despite high KAB concentration there as per geolocated videos. Finally, for the precision of the strikes, I believe the precision is higher in Hulialpole because Ukraine cannot put electronic warfare easily, while the Donbas cities allow multiple EW equipments to be installed. For the precision, you have to take into account that only 5 to 15% of the strikes "hitting something" are in fact hitting their intended target, soldiers, bunkers or trenches.

🇷🇺🇺🇸 In commemoration of the 81st anniversary of Victory in the Great Patriotic War, Russian compatriots living in the United States and concerned Americans held a series of memorial events. They laid wreaths and flowers at memorial sites dedicated to the immortal feat of the Soviet people and the heroic Red Army, which broke the back of Hitler’s war machine in combat brotherhood with the USA and the countries of the anti-Hitler coalition: • the ALSIB heroes memorial in Fairbanks, Alaska; • Fort Richardson National Cemetery in Anchorage, Alaska - the graves of Soviet pilots and sailors who participated in ferrying aircraft to the USSR under the Lend-Lease program; • the monument to Soviet soldiers in Plummer Park, Los Angeles, and the memorial bench in Lincoln Park, San Francisco, California, honoring warriors who fell in World War II battles; • the memorial stone to Red Army soldiers in Beaverton, Oregon, where more than 150 bricks engraved with the names of Soviet veterans have been laid in the park complex; • the burial site of Red Navy sailor M.I.Anisimov at Evergreen Washelli Cemetery in Seattle, Washington; • in Washington, D.C. - the “Spirit of the Elbe” bas-relief and the “Murmansk” inscription dedicated to the Allied Arctic convoys. Following a cherished tradition, activists of the Russian diaspora organized “Immortal Regiment” processions, motorcades, the “St. George’s Ribbon” campaign, meetings with veterans, film screenings, and festive concerts in the states of Washington, Illinois, New York, Connecticut, and Texas. In Florida, they opened the thematic exhibition “We Remember, We Are Proud, We Honor!”, where one of the halls in a Miami bookstore recreated the chronicle of the war years with displays of copies of Soviet publications from 1941–1945. 🎖 We thank everyone who reverently, proudly, and boldly honors the memory of the Soviet soldier-liberator, who saved the world from the brown plague, and refuses to let the combat alliance of our countries during the grim years of the war be forgotten — an alliance that is especially relevant today for normalizing Russian-American relations and for our joint struggle against manifestations of Nazism in modern Europe. Deep bow to the Generation of Heroes! No one is forgotten, nothing is forgotten, and nothing is forgiven!

“Drones upset this entirely. A $100 drone flown by a teenager can take out a lifetime of training and all the support behind it.” Andrew Côté (@Andercot) To be an Armored Knight in the middle ages was a combination warlord, oligarch, and olympic athlete all in one. Training began in youth, at age 12, and required daily practice with sword, lance, pike, on horse and on foot. Longbow men upset this drastically at Agincourt. The armor worn by a knight would cost the same as a large house today, perhaps more, and training was a full time job. To fire a longbow you could be a yeoman, a forester, a skilled peasant, essentially. It did require practice, and started young: from age 12, but practing only one day a week, or a few days a month, mandated by law. Muskets changed this entirely. You could learn to fire a musket in a few weeks of training, and it required no real athleticism. The hardest part was discipline and drill, marching in formation, volley fire, but the weapon itself no longer required a dedicated lifetime of athleticism. Special Forces soldiers are more like knights in the comparative requirements for their athleticism, equipment, and support - for every SF operator theres a dozen or more logistics and support personnel, like squires to a knight. Drones upset this entirely. A $100 drone flown by a teenager can take out a lifetime of training and all the support behind it. They have an extremely low opinion of the US's "hyped" defense companies for being useless in their theater of operations. What wins battles for them is cheap reliable drones produced by the many thousands to millions. China has this. In this April 13th post, I articulated the structural constraints that Iran and the US have in their negotiations. Iran's counter-proposal today and Trump's rejection are operating based on these constraints. Majid Hosseini (@m4h007) As I said before the negotiations, Trump isn’t anywhere near accepting Iran’s terms, nor is America’s political establishment. Trump was desperate to get an off-ramp from his threat, so he pretended to accept Iran’s terms, but went in with his own terms and didn’t make any meaningful concessions. From what I can see these are the constraints on each side: ***Iran*** For Iran, this war and everything that has proceeded it is about its sovereignty. That’s the only lens through which one has to look at Iran from 1979 to today. A revolution, decades of sanctions, and three wars have been the price Iranians have been willing to pay to assert their sovereignty. They could have maintained a nice lifestyle and good relations with the US if they wanted to give up their sovereignty. As such, any trading of sovereignty for comfort would be considered unacceptable for Iranian people. They’ll ask, what was the point of so much suffering, if we wanted to give up any of our rights. What are the issues that directly affect Iran’s sovereignty? Uranium Enrichment: A sovereign right that is part of being an NPT member. Iranians might be willing to give up enrichment for a short few years, in return for major concessions, but more than that is giving up sovereignty and thus deemed unacceptable. Even just a short period will affect training and keeping up with better tools and equipment and thus it’s a very significant concession. Control over the Strait of Hormuz: Iran considers the strait part of its territorial waters and has never conceded broad rights regarding it under any treaty. It treats the strait as a matter of sovereignty, law, and national security. Collecting a toll is something it considers a sovereign matter, not something to be negotiated with others or shared with a non-neighboring party like the US, or other GCC states besides Oman, which shares the other shore. Even the suggestion of such demands would be seen as an attempt to usurp Iranian sovereignty and would be completely unacceptable Support for its allies: This is also a sovereign matter. No country will accept an order from others about which entities to have a relationship with. ***US*** Trump cannot accept Iran’s sovereign rights. Accepting those is an admission of defeat. The entire point of this war has been removing Iran’s sovereignty. This isn’t just about Trump. It’s an institutional constraint within the US. Iran can only exist as a client state, or one that can be attacked at will, or shouldn’t exist altogether. Sovereign equality for Iran is fundamentally unacceptable. I don’t see this constraint changing anytime soon. America’s political system is almost entirely behind this. Even if Trump made such a concession, there’s zero chance it could pass the US congress. Israel is part of the issue, but I don’t believe it’s all because of Israel. As long as the Carter Doctrine hasn’t been completely repudiated, and Persian Gulf hasn’t been conceded to Iran, this won’t change. As such there’s no path to a settlement through negotiations. Perhaps in a generation or two. Soon, consumer prices will force US hand to withdraw from active belligerent status, Iran will officially keep charging a toll for passage through the strait moving forward, and a state of war between Iran and Israel will persist in the background. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/m4h007/status/2043912995865276781#m

🇷🇺🇺🇸 In commemoration of the 81st anniversary of Victory in the Great Patriotic War, Russian compatriots living in the United States and concerned Americans held a series of memorial events. They laid wreaths and flowers at memorial sites dedicated to the immortal feat of the Soviet people and the heroic Red Army, which broke the back of Hitler’s war machine in combat brotherhood with the USA and the countries of the anti-Hitler coalition: • the ALSIB heroes memorial in Fairbanks, Alaska; • Fort Richardson National Cemetery in Anchorage, Alaska - the graves of Soviet pilots and sailors who participated in ferrying aircraft to the USSR under the Lend-Lease program; • the monument to Soviet soldiers in Plummer Park, Los Angeles, and the memorial bench in Lincoln Park, San Francisco, California, honoring warriors who fell in World War II battles; • the memorial stone to Red Army soldiers in Beaverton, Oregon, where more than 150 bricks engraved with the names of Soviet veterans have been laid in the park complex; • the burial site of Red Navy sailor M.I.Anisimov at Evergreen Washelli Cemetery in Seattle, Washington; • in Washington, D.C. - the “Spirit of the Elbe” bas-relief and the “Murmansk” inscription dedicated to the Allied Arctic convoys. Following a cherished tradition, activists of the Russian diaspora organized “Immortal Regiment” processions, motorcades, the “St. George’s Ribbon” campaign, meetings with veterans, film screenings, and festive concerts in the states of Washington, Illinois, New York, Connecticut, and Texas. In Florida, they opened the thematic exhibition “We Remember, We Are Proud, We Honor!”, where one of the halls in a Miami bookstore recreated the chronicle of the war years with displays of copies of Soviet publications from 1941–1945. 🎖 We thank everyone who reverently, proudly, and boldly honors the memory of the Soviet soldier-liberator, who saved the world from the brown plague, and refuses to let the combat alliance of our countries during the grim years of the war be forgotten — an alliance that is especially relevant today for normalizing Russian-American relations and for our joint struggle against manifestations of Nazism in modern Europe. Deep bow to the Generation of Heroes! No one is forgotten, nothing is forgotten, and nothing is forgiven!

Everyone knows about the 300 Spartans at Thermopylae. Almost nothing they know is the full story. Start with the number. There weren't 300 Greeks at that pass. There were around 7,000. Spartans, Thespians, Thebans, Phocians, Locrians, Arcadians, Corinthians. Citizen-soldiers from across Greece who marched north knowing they'd be facing the largest army the ancient world had ever assembled. The 300 is just the headline. The ones who stayed to the end. Now the men themselves. King Leonidas wasn't some chiseled 30-year-old. He was roughly 60 years old when he led that march. And the 300 he picked weren't his strongest warriors. They were specifically men who already had living sons. Spartan law demanded it. Leonidas wasn't choosing an army. He was choosing men whose bloodlines could survive their deaths. Every one of them knew what that meant before they ever saw a Persian. They marched anyway. And they didn't march alone in the way movies suggest. Each Spartan citizen-soldier was accompanied by helots, the enslaved underclass that propped up the entire Spartan economy, outnumbering their masters roughly seven to one. Hundreds of helots fought and died at Thermopylae too. They get no statues. No films. No name on the monument. The pass itself was barely 15 meters wide in 480 BC (it's silted up now and looks nothing like it did then). That bottleneck is the only reason a few thousand men could hold off a Persian force modern historians estimate at 70,000 to 300,000. Herodotus said 1.7 million. He was lying, or possibly counting cooks, slaves, and camp followers, but even the conservative number is staggering. For two days, they held. Wave after wave broken against bronze and discipline. Xerxes reportedly leapt from his throne three times in fury watching his men die. He sent in the Immortals, his elite personal guard, supposedly invincible. They weren't. Not in that pass. Then the Greeks were betrayed. A local man named Ephialtes, whose name still means "nightmare" in modern Greek, sold the Persians a goat path through the mountains that flanked the pass. The Phocians assigned to guard it scattered when the Immortals appeared in the dawn fog. Leonidas knew by morning he was surrounded. He dismissed most of the allied Greek forces. Saved their lives. But here's what almost nobody talks about: roughly 700 Thespians, led by a man named Demophilus, refused to leave. They were citizen-farmers from a small town that knew Persia was coming for them next no matter what. They chose to die beside the Spartans rather than run. About 400 Thebans stayed too, though their motives were murkier and many surrendered when the end came. So the "last stand of the 300" was actually closer to 1,500 men. The Thespians died to the last. Their town was burned to the ground by the Persians weeks later anyway. They're a footnote in a story that should bear their name. The final fight happened on a small hill called Kolonos. Spears shattered. Swords broken. Herodotus says they fought with hands and teeth at the end. Leonidas fell early, and the Spartans fought four times over his body to keep the Persians from taking it. They lost. Xerxes had Leonidas decapitated and his body crucified, a violation of Persian custom so extreme it tells you exactly how badly that old man had humiliated the king of kings. Forty years later, Sparta sent a delegation to recover his bones and bring him home. Two Spartans survived the battle. One, Aristodemus, had been sent away with an eye infection. He returned to Sparta and was treated as a coward, shunned, refused fire, refused conversation, until he threw himself into the front line at Plataea a year later and died seeking redemption. The other survivor, Pantites, was sent on a diplomatic errand and missed the fight. He hanged himself from the shame. That's the world they lived in. The epitaph carved at the site doesn't brag. It doesn't even mention victory, because there wasn't one. Roughly translated, it just asks the traveler to tell Sparta that her sons died here, obedient to her laws. A small group of farmers, an old king, an enslaved underclass written out of history, and a town that vanished from the map. Together, for three days in August of 480 BC, they did the math on freedom and decided the price was worth it. We remember 300 of them. There were always more.
